sections.h2: Ways to sell a Federal Way house
sections.html:
Three paths are open to a Federal Way owner: hire an agent, handle the sale personally, or hand the keys to a buyer who needs no mortgage. Weigh the house's shape, your moving date and what you still owe the lender.

  • Agent listing: expect to tidy up, host showings and haggle over inspection findings. The audience is biggest, and so is the wait.
  • Going solo: you set the price, advertise, and complete the state's seller disclosure statement yourself.
  • Direct cash purchase: without a bank in the middle, a declined loan cannot derail closing. Compare the written offer with what you would pocket after your payoff, taxes and repair spending.

sections.h2: Federal Way housing at a glance
sections.html:
Federal Way occupies the southwest corner of King County, roughly 25 miles south of Seattle, with 99,729 residents. The count is 1.3 percent lower than in 2020, so the city is not adding people. Around 45 percent of occupied homes are rentals. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $552,800, a citywide midpoint worth using only as a loose starting reference.

Green space adds appeal in some neighborhoods. Steel Lake Park is on South 312th Street, Lake Killarney is close by, and Dash Point State Park is the one developed waterfront park within city limits. A cabin from 1883 in West Hylebos Wetlands Park is the oldest known building in town.

A few eastern areas, including Star Lake, Camelot, Lakeland and Jovita, were named potential annexation areas. Confirm your parcel is inside the city before you call the Permit Center. The city's maps, the King County Parcel Viewer or the Permit Center itself can all supply a parcel number.

This one is the seller's bill. RCW 82.45.080 assigns Washington's real estate excise tax to the seller, payable to the county treasurer as of the sale date even if recording happens later. For a Federal Way deed, that treasurer is King County's.

Rates climb with price. The Department of Revenue currently shows 1.1 percent up to $525,000, then 1.28 percent to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent to $3,025,000, and 3 percent beyond. For sales on or after January 1, 2027 the breakpoints become $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Cities add a local rate, which your escrow officer can quote for your parcel.

A month after the sale, penalty and interest start accruing, and a lien can follow an unpaid balance. Have escrow print the excise tax on its own line of your settlement statement.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit or approval before selling a Federal Way house?
sections.html:
Building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, demolition and fire prevention permits, plus land use and sign permits, all go through the City of Federal Way Permit Center. It is the place to ask about repairs you want to finish before listing, or about work a former owner may have done unpermitted.

  • Phone and email: 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov.
  • Hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Wednesdays and city holidays, the day after Thanksgiving among them, the public counter is shut.
  • Applications: request a Document Upload Link, which may take a few days, and submit reviewable plans electronically. Residential electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits can also be filed online through My Building Permit.

Be wary of an email that claims to be from the city and asks for a wire transfer. The city does not do that, so phone the Permit Center before sending money.

sections.h2: Property taxes on a Federal Way house
sections.html:
The first installment comes due April 30 and the second October 31. Under RCW 84.56.020 the county treasurer collects, which means King County. Pull the current statement for your parcel before listing, since title work will reveal any open balance. If you pay through a lender, still check the county record yourself so nothing surprises you at the closing table.

If closing falls mid-period, escrow divides the bill between you and the buyer. Confirm your latest payment has posted first, so the division starts from the right figure.

Drivers reach Interstate 5 at the 348th Street, 320th Street and 272nd Street exits, and State Route 99, the Pacific Highway, cuts through town. Buses from King County Metro, Pierce Transit and Sound Transit Express stop at the Federal Way Transit Center on 23rd Avenue South, and the Link light rail extension to Federal Way Downtown station opened in December 2025. Commutes average 32.1 minutes, which makes quick freeway and station access worth advertising.

Federal Way Public Schools runs the local district. In your listing, mention the closest park, the nearest I-5 exit and how long the trip to the station takes.

sections.h2: What to check before you accept an offer
sections.html:
Offers can look alike on paper and still differ by thousands once costs are added up. Go through this list with each one.

  • Insist on a written offer listing price, closing date and the party responsible for each closing cost.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff statement showing the precise balance.
  • Have the buyer prove funds, and learn whether repairs or an inspection can change the deal.
  • Run the excise tax rates above, then ask escrow for the local rate.
  • Clarify whether the house must be cleared out, and by when.
  • Rank routes by the money you would walk away with, not by the advertised price.

If a tenant lives in the house, read the lease before promising a closing date, since a buyer will need to know who occupies the home and for how long.

Under RCW 64.06.020, a seller of improved residential property owes the buyer a finished disclosure statement. The clock is five business days from acceptance of a written contract, and a buyer may waive the form or the transfer may be exempt. Once it arrives, the buyer has three business days to back out.

Answer only from your own knowledge of the roof, plumbing, sewer and past repairs. A folder holding permit history, loan payoff and tax statement makes the form faster to fill in and buyer follow-ups easier to answer. Cash buyers ask the same things, just without an appraiser or underwriter second-guessing the replies.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax on a house sale in Federal Way?
faqs.a: The seller, under RCW 82.45.080. If the seller leaves it unpaid, responsibility shifts to the buyer and a lien may attach to the property.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Federal Way house?
faqs.a: Half is due April 30 and half October 31, paid through King County. Request the latest statement for your parcel from the county.

faqs.q: Which county is Federal Way in?
faqs.a: King County, in its southwest corner about 25 miles south of Seattle. Deeds, excise tax affidavits and property tax bills for a Federal Way home all run through King County offices.

faqs.q: How do I find my parcel number in Federal Way?
faqs.a: Look it up on the city's maps or the King County Parcel Viewer, or ask the Permit Center at 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov. Permit questions and title work both call for it.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Most sellers do. The finished form is due five business days after a written contract is accepted, unless it is waived or the transfer is exempt. Three business days after delivery, the buyer's right to rescind ends.
